info.title: Suplex AgentApi Runtime API
info.description: Version v1 is additive-only within a major version. Pairing, credential rotation, and administration are separate provisioning APIs and are not part of this contract. Company, project grants, and creator ownership come from current server persistence, never request fields. Reads cover every task in the agent's currently granted projects. Commands, dependency writes, and delivery operations remain creator-only. Denied company, grant, and missing-resource reads are all non-enumerating 404 responses.

post.summary: Create a backlog or queued task
post.description: Creates a backlog task. With queue true, the task is queued: it starts now when every prerequisite is complete, and otherwise stays queued with zero sessions until the last prerequisite completes. Without queue, it never starts by itself. dryRun true validates the same request and returns its projection without writing a task, dependency, receipt, artifact, or audit event. The server defaults description to an empty string and rejects unknown fields with request_invalid. dependsOn sets the prerequisites, shown as Blocked by. A prerequisite can be any task the agent can read in a granted project. The task waits for the prerequisite. A prerequisite task is complete when it is delivered. For a pull_request_draft, pull_request_ready, or merged target, its pull request must also merge. A self-reference, a cycle, or a task outside a granted project is rejected. Idempotency is scoped to the paired agent and company. An identical replay returns 200; reuse for a different request returns 409 with idempotency_conflict. GET /api/agent/tasks supports opaque cursors and returns nextCursor.

get.summary: Read a task in a granted project
get.description: A paired agent can read every task in its currently granted company projects. Task states are backlog, queued, active, waiting_human, cancelled, and delivered. queue.waitingOn lists the exact wait reason of each incomplete prerequisite. A prerequisite is complete when it is delivered at its own delivery target; the pull_request_draft, pull_request_ready, and merged targets also need the merged pull request state Suplex observed from GitHub. Human questions are records only: answering them remains human authority and no agent answer command exists. The server router rejects path parameters longer than 100 characters before this authenticated operation is matched; those router-level responses are outside this contract.

patch.summary: Change the details of a backlog or queued task
patch.description: Changes the details of a backlog or queued task: title, description, workflow, Coordinator, Worker, Advisor profiles, delivery target, project tests, and screenshots. Every update requires the current task revision and an idempotency key, and names at least one field. An omitted field keeps its stored value. workflowId names a workflow from GET /api/agent/workflows; Suplex applies its engine. advisorProfileIds is the complete Advisor selection: an empty object clears named Advisors, so each role follows its default. Each named role must belong to the task's resulting workflow, and each profile must be an existing Coordinator profile. A queued task stays queued with the same prerequisites. To hold a queued task while it changes, send disarm_task, update the task, then send start_task to queue it again. An active or delivered task accepts only deliveryTarget, moved forward: Suplex sets the new target and the Coordinator continues toward it, reopening a delivered task. A waiting_human, cancelled, or archived task is refused with illegal_command. A rejected profile or workflow reports field, value, and reason, and the task keeps its revision. The response is the updated task with its new revision.

put.summary: Replace the prerequisites of a task
put.description: Replaces dependsOn, shown as Blocked by, with the complete set in the body. A prerequisite can be any task the agent can read in a granted project. The task waits for the prerequisite. A prerequisite task is complete when it is delivered. For a pull_request_draft, pull_request_ready, or merged target, its pull request must also merge. A self-reference, a cycle, or a task outside a granted project is rejected. dryRun true validates the replacement and reports the projected prerequisites and start state without changing dependencies, queue state, or audits. A self-reference, a cycle, or an unavailable task is rejected and the current set stays. Unknown fields are rejected. The response and every later read report dependsOn and blockedBy from the same stored edges.

The complete set replaces the current set; an empty array removes every prerequisite.

post.summary: Apply an authorized task lifecycle command
post.description: Only the paired agent that created the task can send a command. Every command requires the current task revision and an idempotency key. A change to only updatedAt or delivery does not make a revision stale. answer_human_question also needs questionId and exactly one of optionId or answer. It fails with answer_grant_required until an administrator grants the agent permission, with question_stale for an old questionId, with task_not_waiting when the task has no question, and with human_decision_required for a task limit decision or command cleanup. start_task queues a manual backlog task: it starts now when every prerequisite is complete and never bypasses one. disarm_task returns a queued task to the manual backlog. taskCommands lists exactly the lifecycle commands accepted by suplex_command_task. autonomousCommands also includes task creation and, when enabled, runtime delivery commands. A paired agent can answer a task's Coordinator question with answer_human_question only after an administrator lets it answer on their behalf. Task limit decisions and command cleanup confirmations stay with a person. The runtime API exposes delivery and merge commands only when capabilities reports them. Suplex can perform delivery for a task's configured target, including a merge after review, without an agent command.

questionId.description: The current question id from the task's question.id. Only answer_human_question accepts it.

optionId.description: An offered option id from question.options, such as option-1. Send optionId or answer, not both.

answer.description: A free-text answer. Send optionId or answer, not both.
